Class.name: BIExport.DashboardExport
Class.Description: Pure ObjectScript (no Python): resolves every pivot widget on a saved dashboard into the same normalized export structure BIExport.MDXExport already produces for a single pivot, so BIExport.XLSXWriter's BuildMultiSheetXLSX can turn a whole dashboard into one workbook - one sheet per pivot widget - without any of the cellset-flattening logic being duplicated. BuildDashboardExportData is this class's only public entry point; everything else is a private helper for it. Resolving a saved pivot into a live, queryable %DeepSee.Component.pivotTable uses the exact same %OpenFolderItem + %CopyToComponent sequence %DeepSee.Component.Widget.pivot's own %LoadPivotInfo uses (confirmed live by dumping that method's compiled source) - but here the %DeepSee.Component.pivotTable is a plain, page-less %New() object, never attached to any Zen component tree. That side-steps the live-component property-read trap BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot had to work around (reading a property off a component already wired into a rendering page's tree can throw

Method.name: BuildDashboardExportData
Method.Description:
Opens the dashboard named by <var>pDashboardFullName</var> (its full library path, e.g. "BIExport Test Dashboard.dashboard") and returns a <class>%DynamicObject</class> shaped like: <example> { "title": "...", // the dashboard's own title property "dashboardName": "...", // its fullName, echoed back "sheets": [ {"widgetName":"Widget1", "title":"...", "data": { ...BuildExportData() shape... }}, {"widgetName":"Widget2", "title":"...", "error": "..."} // widget that failed ], "skipped": [ {"widgetName":"Widget3", "title":"...", "type":"..."} // non-pivot widget ] } </example> One sheet entry per pivot-family widget (see <method>%IsPivotWidgetType</method>) - present even if that widget's own export failed, with an "error" field instead of "data" so one bad widget can't take down the whole export. Non-pivot-family widgets (chart-catalog/KPI/text) never get a sheet entry at all; they're listed separately under "skipped" purely so <class>BIExport.XLSXWriter</class> can mention them by name on the combined Info sheet, per the plan's "clear message, not a bug" call.
<var>pStatus</var> is $$$OK unless the dashboard itself couldn't be opened at all - an individual widget failure is recorded on its own sheet entry instead, never surfaced through <var>pStatus</var>.

Method.name: %IsPivotWidgetType
Method.Description: True if <var>pType</var> (a widget's own <property>type</property>) is something resolvable the same way <class>%DeepSee.Dashboard.Widget::%CreateVisualWidget</class> resolves it into a real class (blank/"pivot" prefixed to "%DeepSee.Component.Widget.pivot"; anything containing a dot used as a literal class name - same prefixing rule <class>BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot</class>'s own doc comment already documents) AND that resolved class actually extends <class>%DeepSee.Component.Widget.pivot</class>. More general than <class>BIExport.DashboardTools</class>'s own <method>%IsPivotFamily</method> (which only needs to recognize its own conversion source/target literal strings) - this one needs to correctly classify ANY pivot-widget subclass a dashboard might already be using, not just the one this package ships.
Method.Implementation: If (pType = "") || (pType = "pivot") Quit 1 Set tClass = $Select(pType[".":pType, 1:"%DeepSee.Component.Widget."_pType) Quit ##class(%Dictionary.CompiledClass).%ExistsId(tClass) && $ClassMethod(tClass, "%Extends", "%DeepSee.Component.Widget.pivot")

Method.name: %BuildWidgetSheet
Method.Description: Resolves one pivot-family widget's saved pivot into a sheet entry - see <method>BuildDashboardExportData</method>'s doc comment for the shape. Never throws; any failure (missing/bad saved pivot, MDX error) is caught and recorded as this sheet's own "error" field instead.

Class.name: BIExport.DashboardTools
Class.Description:
Rollout helper for opting existing dashboards into the real .xlsx/JSON export widget (<class>BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot</class>) without hand-editing dashboard XML - same idea as <class>BIExport.Favorites</class> (a helper method instead of a manual edit), but this one rewrites a dashboard's own widget definitions rather than adding a Portal bookmark.
A widget's rendering class is just a string property on its definition - <property>%DeepSee.Dashboard.Widget::type</property> - confirmed live (dumping <method>%DeepSee.Dashboard.Widget::%CreateVisualWidget</method>'s compiled source) to be instantiated directly by that method, prefixed with "%DeepSee.Component.Widget." unless it already contains a dot. So converting a widget is just: open the dashboard, find the widget by its stable <property>name</property> (not <property>key</property>, which is an unstable hash regenerated on layout changes), set <property>type</property> to "BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot", <method>%Save</method> the dashboard.
Verified end-to-end live (Playwright) against a scratch clone of "Basic Dashboard Demo.dashboard" before this class was written: cloning via <method>%ConstructClone</method>(1) + re-<method>%Save</method>-ing under a new <property>fullName</property> creates a genuinely independent copy (new %Id), and flipping a widget's <property>type</property> (even to a nonexistent class, as a stress test) + <method>%Save</method> + reload reliably round-trips - the dashboard viewer surfaced a clean in-page error for the bogus class and rendered normally again once the type was fixed, with no corruption either way.

Method.name: ConvertWidget
Method.Description: Converts one widget (identified by its <property>name</property>, e.g. "Widget1" - see the Widgets tab of the Dashboard Editor, or dump <property>widgets</property> in a Terminal, for the current names) on the dashboard named by <var>pDashboardFullName</var> (its full library path, e.g. "Basic Dashboard Demo.dashboard") to <var>pNewType</var>. Refuses to convert a widget whose current <property>type</property> isn't recognizably in the stock pivot-widget family (bare "pivot", blank, or already <var>pNewType</var>/"BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot") - chart-only/KPI/text widget types have no confirmed compatibility with this class's <method>%OnCreateControls</method> override and aren't a supported target.

Method.name: ConvertAllWidgets
Method.Description: Same as <method>ConvertWidget</method>, but converts every widget on the dashboard whose current <property>type</property> is in the recognized pivot-widget family (see <method>%IsPivotFamily</method>) in one call. Widgets outside that family (chart-only, KPI, text, etc.) are silently skipped rather than erroring the whole call - a dashboard mixing pivot and non-pivot widgets is the normal case, not a mistake.

Method.name: RevertWidget
Method.Description: Sets a single widget's <property>type</property> back to the stock "pivot" - the inverse of <method>ConvertWidget</method>, for backing out the change on a dashboard that turns out not to want it.

Method.name: %IsPivotFamily
Method.Description: True if <var>pType</var> (a widget's current <property>type</property> value) is something this class is willing to convert: blank or bare "pivot" (the stock default, prefixed to %DeepSee.Component.Widget.pivot by %CreateVisualWidget), or already <var>pTargetType</var>/"BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot" (idempotent re-conversion). Anything else - a chart-only, KPI, text widget, or some other custom subclass - is not a confirmed-safe target and is treated as not-pivot-family.
Method.Implementation: Quit (pType = "") || (pType = "pivot") || (pType = pTargetType) || (pType = "BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot")

Class.name: BIExport.Favorites
Class.Description:
Adds a "Favorite" bookmark in the IRIS BI User Portal (the same Favorites list shown on the Analyzer/Home page) that opens a saved pivot through <class>BIExport.UI.Analyzer</class> instead of the stock <class>%DeepSee.UI.Analyzer</class> - so the Export dropdown's "Excel Workbook"/"JSON" options are there without needing to change any existing link/shortcut URL. Implemented as a <class>%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Link</class> folder item (the same mechanism the Portal's own "New Link" dialog uses), favorited for the current user via <class>%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Utils</class>.
See README.md, "Add a Favorites bookmark instead" for usage from the Analyzer's own "Show MDX" pivot name, or call directly from a Terminal: <example> Do ##class(BIExport.Favorites).AddAnalyzerFavorite("HoleFoods/By Region.pivot") </example>

Method.name: AddAnalyzerFavorite
Method.Description: Creates (or updates) a <class>%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Link</class> pointing at <class>BIExport.UI.Analyzer</class> for the saved pivot named by <var>pPivotFullName</var> (its full library path, e.g. "HoleFoods/By Region.pivot" - the same value shown as "fullName" in the Portal's pivot list), and adds it to the current user's ($UserName) Favorites. <var>pFolderName</var> controls which folder the bookmark itself is filed under (created if missing); <var>pTitle</var> defaults to the pivot's own item name.
Method.Implementation:
Set tSC = $$$OK Try { If (pPivotFullName = "") { Set tSC = $$$ERROR($$$GeneralError, "pPivotFullName is required, e.g. ""HoleFoods/By Region.pivot""") Quit } Set tSC = ##class(%DeepSee.UserLibrary.FolderItem).%ParseFullName(pPivotFullName, .tFolder, .tItemName, .tExt) If $$$ISERR(tSC) Quit Set:pTitle="" pTitle = tItemName
Set tHref = "BIExport.UI.Analyzer.cls?PIVOT=" _ $ZCVT($ZCVT(pPivotFullName, "O", "UTF8"), "O", "URL")
Set tLink = ##class(%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Link).%New() Set tLink.fullName = pFolderName _ "/" _ pTitle Set tLink.href = tHref Set tLink.title = pTitle Set tLink.description = "Opens '" _ pPivotFullName _ "' via BIExport.UI.Analyzer.cls (adds Excel Workbook/JSON export options to the Export dropdown)." Set tLink.owner = $UserName Set tLink.public = 1 Set tSC = tLink.%Save() If $$$ISERR(tSC) Quit
Set tSC = ##class(%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Utils).%AddFavorite(tLink.fullName) If $$$ISERR(tSC) Quit
Write "Added favorite: ", tLink.fullName, " -> ", tHref, ! } Catch ex { Set tSC = ex.AsStatus() } Quit tSC

Method.name: RemoveAnalyzerFavorite
Method.Description: Removes the bookmark from the current user's Favorites list (does not delete the underlying <class>%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Link</class> item - same as unfavoriting from the Portal UI). Pass the same <var>pFolderName</var>/<var>pTitle</var> used with <method>AddAnalyzerFavorite</method> (or the exact bookmark fullName as <var>pTitle</var> with <var>pFolderName</var>="").
Method.Implementation: Set tLink = ##class(%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Link).%New() Set tLink.fullName = $S(pFolderName="":"", 1:pFolderName_"/") _ pTitle Quit ##class(%DeepSee.UserLibrary.Utils).%RemoveFavorite(tLink.fullName)

Class.name: BIExport.MDXExport
Class.Description: Executes an MDX query and flattens the resulting cellset (or drillthrough listing) into a normalized, JSON-friendly structure that <class>BIExport.XLSXWriter</class> (or any other renderer) can consume without needing to know anything about %DeepSee.ResultSet. Mirrors the cellset-walking logic used by the stock Analyzer export buttons (%DeepSee.UI.MDXExcel / %DeepSee.Component.deepseeCSVProvider) but keeps real values/types instead of pre-formatting everything as HTML/CSV text.

Method.name: BuildExportData
Method.Description: pOptions supported keys (all optional): title, subtitle - %String, printed above the table cube - %String, cube name/caption - shown on the Info sheet even when title is blank (e.g. an ad-hoc pivot that was never saved, so has no name to show) listing - %String, listing name to use if the MDX is a drillthrough/listing query rowTotals - %Boolean, include a "Total" column (one value per row, summed across columns) - default false. Independent of columnTotals; a pivot can have either, both, or neither turned on, and this must mirror that exactly rather than OR-ing them into one flag (doing so was a bug - see BIExport.UI.Analyzer's buildExportURL()). columnTotals - %Boolean, include a "Total" row (one value per column, summed down rows) - default false. Independent of rowTotals. rowTotalAgg - %String, aggregation function for rowTotals - one of "sum" (default), "count", "min", "max", "avg", "pct" (% of total). Passed straight through to %DeepSee.ResultSet's %GetRowTotal - these are exactly the values its pAgg parameter accepts, and also exactly the <option value="..."> values in the Pivot Options dialog's Summary aggregation dropdown, so no translation is needed at either end. columnTotalAgg - %String, aggregation function for columnTotals - same values as rowTotalAgg, passed to %GetColumnTotal. filters - array of {name, value} objects, printed as a recap block rowCaptions - the row axis's dimension/level captions (e.g. "YearSold", "Product Category"), outermost first. The ResultSet API has no way to derive these itself - they're metadata the pivot table widget already has client-side (this is exactly what the stock exportExcel() passes as ROWCAPTIONS, sourced from table.getRowCaptions().join('\n') - see BIExport.UI.Analyzer's buildExportURL()). Accepts either a %DynamicArray of strings or a single "\n"-delimited %String in that same format.

Method.name: %ParseFilterPairs
Method.Description: Builds a filters array (in the {name,value} shape BuildExportData's "filters" option expects) from two parallel "\n"-delimited strings - the same shape XLSXPage.cls/JSONPage.cls receive via FILTERNAMES/FILTERVALUES query params, sourced from the pivot table widget's own table.getFilterInfo() client-side (mirroring what stock exportExcel() does with those same two arrays).
Method.Implementation: Set tResult = [] If (pNames = "") Quit tResult Set tCount = $Length(pNames,$C(10)) For i=1:1:tCount { Do tResult.%Push({"name": ($Piece(pNames,$C(10),i)), "value": ($Piece(pValues,$C(10),i))}) } Quit tResult

Method.name: %ParseCaptions
Method.Description: Normalizes pValue (either a %DynamicArray of strings, or a single "\n"-delimited %String) into a %ListOfDataTypes of caption strings, outermost first.

Method.name: %StrOrNull
Method.Implementation: Quit $Select($IsObject($Get(pValue)):"",1:$Get(pValue,""))

Method.name: %BuildListing
Method.Description: Flattens a drillthrough/listing result into {columns:[{name,numeric}], rows:[[...]]}

Method.name: %BuildCellset
Method.Description: Flattens an MDX cellset into headers + typed data cells (+ optional totals). pRowTotals and pColTotals are independent - see BuildExportData's doc comment.

Method.name: %MakeCell
Method.Description: Builds a typed cell object {t, v, fmt} from a raw MDX cell value + MDX format string.

Method.name: %MakeNumericCell
%TranslateFormat
Method.Description: Translates an MDX/ODBC-style number format string (e.g. "#,#0.00", "$#,#0") into a standard Excel number_format string. Real xlsx formats don't need the backslash escaping the legacy HTML "mso-number-format" trick required.
Method.Implementation:
If (pFormat = "") Quit "#,##0"
Set tHasPercent = (pFormat["%") Set tHasComma = (pFormat[",") Set tHasDollar = (pFormat["$")
Set tScale = 0 Set tDot = $Find(pFormat,".") If (tDot) { Set p = tDot While $Case($Extract(pFormat,p),"#":1,"0":1,:0) { Set tScale = tScale + 1 Set p = p + 1 } }
Set tInt = $Select(tHasComma:"#,##0",1:"0") Set tOut = $Select(tScale>0:tInt_"."_$Translate($Justify("",tScale)," ","0"),1:tInt) Set:tHasDollar tOut = "$"_tOut Set:tHasPercent tOut = tOut_"%" Quit tOut

wb = openpyxl.Workbook() ws = wb.active ws.title = "Test" ws["A1"] = "Hello" ws["B1"] = 42 ws["B1"].number_format = "#,##0"
buf = io.BytesIO() wb.save(buf) return buf.getvalue()

Class.name: BIExport.REST
Class.Description: REST service exposing real-file BI exports (starting with genuine .xlsx, replacing the Analyzer's HTML-saved-as-.xls behavior). See CLAUDE.md for the design rationale and docs/iris-environment.md for how this is deployed.

XData.name: UrlMap
XData.Data: <Routes> <Route Url="/xlsx" Method="POST" Call="ExportXLSX"/> <Route Url="/json" Method="POST" Call="ExportJSON"/> </Routes>

Method.name: ExportXLSX
Method.Description: POST body (JSON): { "mdx": "<MDX query text>", - required "filename": "report.xlsx", - optional, defaults to "<title>.xlsx", or "<cube>_<timestamp>.xlsx" if no title "title": "...", "subtitle": "...", - optional, shown on the Info sheet "cube": "HoleFoods Sales", - optional, shown on the Info sheet even with no title, and used in the default filename "listing": "ListingName", - optional, for drillthrough/listing MDX "rowTotals": true, - optional, include a "Total" column (per-row sums) "columnTotals": true, - optional, include a "Total" row (per-column sums) - independent of rowTotals; a pivot can have either, both, or neither "rowTotalAgg": "avg", - optional, aggregation for rowTotals: "sum" (default), "count", "min", "max", "avg", "pct" "columnTotalAgg": "avg", - optional, aggregation for columnTotals, same values "filters": [{"name":"...","value":"..."}] - optional, recap block on the Info sheet "rowCaptions": ["YearSold", ...] - optional, row axis dimension captions (outermost first) for the row-header columns; the MDX/ ResultSet API can't derive these on its own - this is metadata an external caller would need to already know from how it built the MDX } Returns 503 (text/plain body, not a raw exception dump) if <class>BIExport.XLSXWriter</class>'s <method>IsAvailable</method> reports IRIS Embedded Python/openpyxl aren't available - see that method's doc comment. /json below has no such check; it needs no Python at all.
Method.Implementation:
Set tSC = $$$OK Try { If '##class(BIExport.XLSXWriter).IsAvailable(.tReason) { Set %response.Status = "503 Service Unavailable" Set %response.ContentType = "text/plain" Write tReason Quit }
Set tBody = %request.Content Do tBody.Rewind() Set tJSONIn = tBody.Read(tBody.Size)
Set tReq = {}.%FromJSON(tJSONIn) Set tMDX = tReq.%Get("mdx", "") If (tMDX = "") { Set %response.Status = "400 Bad Request" Write "Missing required 'mdx' field" Quit }
Set tData = ##class(BIExport.MDXExport).BuildExportData(tMDX, tReq) Set tJSON = tData.%ToJSON() Set tBytes = ##class(BIExport.XLSXWriter).BuildXLSX(tJSON)
Set tFileName = tReq.%Get("filename", ..%DefaultFileName(tReq, "xlsx"))
Set %response.ContentType = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet" Do %response.SetHeader("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=""" _ tFileName _ """")
Set tStream = ##class(%Stream.TmpBinary).%New() Do tStream.Write(tBytes) Do tStream.Rewind() Do tStream.OutputToDevice() } Catch ex { Set %response.Status = "500 Internal Server Error" Set %response.ContentType = "text/plain" Write ex.DisplayString() } Quit $$$OK

Method.name: ExportJSON
Method.Description: POST body (JSON): same fields as /xlsx (mdx, filename, title, subtitle, listing, rowTotals, columnTotals, filters) - returns BIExport.MDXExport's normalized structure as-is. No Python involved: %DynamicObject already has %ToJSON(), so this is pure ObjectScript.
Method.Implementation:
Set tSC = $$$OK Try { Set tBody = %request.Content Do tBody.Rewind() Set tJSONIn = tBody.Read(tBody.Size)
Set tReq = {}.%FromJSON(tJSONIn) Set tMDX = tReq.%Get("mdx", "") If (tMDX = "") { Set %response.Status = "400 Bad Request" Write "Missing required 'mdx' field" Quit }
Set tData = ##class(BIExport.MDXExport).BuildExportData(tMDX, tReq)
Set tFileName = tReq.%Get("filename", ..%DefaultFileName(tReq, "json"))
Set %response.ContentType = "application/json" Do %response.SetHeader("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=""" _ tFileName _ """")
Do tData.%ToJSON() } Catch ex { Set %response.Status = "500 Internal Server Error" Set %response.ContentType = "text/plain" Write ex.DisplayString() } Quit $$$OK

Method.name: %DefaultFileName
Method.Description: Filename to use when the caller didn't supply one: "<title>.<ext>" if a title was given, else "<cube or 'export'>_<short timestamp>.<ext>" - matches BIExport.UI.Analyzer.buildExportURL()'s fallback for an ad-hoc pivot with no saved name to hang a filename on, so repeated title-less exports don't all collide on a single literal "export.xlsx".
Method.Implementation: Set tTitle = pReq.%Get("title", "") If (tTitle '= "") { Quit tTitle _ "." _ pExt } Set tCube = pReq.%Get("cube", "") Set tBase = $Select(tCube'="":tCube,1:"export") Set tTS = $TR($ZDate($H,8),"-") _ "-" _ $Extract($TR($ZTime($Piece($H,",",2),1),":"),1,4) Quit tBase _ "_" _ tTS _ "." _ pExt

Class.name: BIExport.UI.Analyzer
Class.Description:
Thin subclass of the stock BI Analyzer page that adds real "Excel Workbook" (.xlsx) and "JSON" options to the existing Export dropdown (alongside Excel/CSV/CSV with Heading), calling <class>BIExport.UI.XLSXPage</class>/<class>BIExport.UI.JSONPage</class> instead of the HTML-saved-as-.xls exporter.
Reachable at the same CSP application as the stock page, just under this class's name instead of the "_DeepSee.UI.Analyzer.zen" alias, e.g. /csp/<namespace>/BIExport.UI.Analyzer.cls?CUBE=... - point any links/shortcuts at this URL instead of the stock one to pick up the new options.

Parameter.name: ANALYZERURL
Parameter.Description: The stock page hardcodes this to "_DeepSee.UI.Analyzer.zen", which seeds the client-side <var>analyzerURL</var> property that every navigation action (open pivot from the tree, the "Open" popup, Save-As, cube/SubjectArea change, New Pivot, Restore Pivot) uses to build its redirect URL. Left unoverridden, every one of those actions bounces back to the stock Analyzer page instead of staying on this subclass. Override with this class's own URL so navigation stays here.

Method.name: onloadHandler
Method.Description: Runs after the stock page finishes its own load logic; DOM-patches the existing Export dropdown to add "Excel Workbook" and "JSON" items - grayed out (no click handler, hover text explaining why) instead of wired up if <method>IsXLSXAvailable</method> reports IRIS Embedded Python/openpyxl aren't available; "JSON" is never affected, since it has no Python dependency. Implemented as a DOM patch (rather than duplicating the dropdown-building code) so it keeps working even if the stock page's internal markup/ids change across versions.
Method.Implementation: this.invokeSuper('onloadHandler', arguments); this.addExtraExportOptions();

Method.name: IsXLSXAvailable
Method.Description: Synchronous server round-trip so addExtraExportOptions (pure client JS, no other server call at all) can gray out "Excel Workbook" the same way the guaranteed server-side surfaces already do. Confirmed live (Playwright: zenPage.IsXLSXAvailable() called with no callback argument returned its value synchronously, no async round-trip needed) that this IRIS version's Zen executes a ZenMethod call synchronously when the client-side stub is invoked without a callback function - the plan this class was built from treated this as best-effort/unverified going in; it verified cleanly, so it's used directly rather than falling back. Returns "1" if BIExport.XLSXWriter.IsAvailable is true, else "0|<reason>" - packed into one string rather than an Output parameter, since a synchronous ZenMethod call only gets back its one return value, never a by-reference argument.
Method.Implementation: Set tOK = ##class(BIExport.XLSXWriter).IsAvailable(.tReason) Quit $Select(tOK:"1",1:"0|"_tReason)

Method.name: addExtraExportOptions
exportXLSX
Method.Description: Opens the real .xlsx export page for the current pivot. See buildExportURL for why this opens a same-application CSP page instead of calling BIExport.REST.
Method.Implementation: var url = this.buildExportURL('BIExport.UI.XLSXPage.cls', 'xlsx'); if (url) { window.open(url, 'xlsx', ''); }

Method.name: exportJSON
Method.Description: Opens the JSON export page for the current pivot. See buildExportURL for why this opens a same-application CSP page instead of calling BIExport.REST.
Method.Implementation: var url = this.buildExportURL('BIExport.UI.JSONPage.cls', 'json'); if (url) { window.open(url, 'json', ''); }

Method.name: buildExportURL
Method.Description: Mirrors exportExcel()'s gathering of the current pivot's MDX/title, but points at one of our own plain CSP pages (in this SAME application, not the separate BIExport.REST application) so the browser's existing Analyzer login session covers it - exactly the same reason exportExcel() itself uses window.open() to a sibling page rather than a cross-application fetch. Shared by exportXLSX()/exportJSON(); pPage is the target page class name, pExtension the default filename extension.

Class.name: BIExport.UI.DashboardViewer
Class.Description: Subclass of the stock dashboard viewer page that adds a real, whole-dashboard multi-sheet ".xlsx" export - one workbook with one sheet per pivot widget (see BIExport.DashboardExport/BIExport.XLSXWriter.BuildMultiSheetXLSX) - next to the per-widget "Excel Workbook"/"JSON" options BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot already adds to each widget's own export dropdown. Reachable at the same CSP application as the stock page, just under this class's name instead of "_DeepSee.UserPortal.DashboardViewer.zen", e.g. /csp//BIExport.UI.DashboardViewer.cls?DASHBOARD=... - point any existing shortcuts/links at this URL instead of the stock one to pick up the new option. DEVIATION FROM PLAN: the plan's sketch assumed an existing page-level "icon stack" to inject a new standalone toolbar icon next to - confirmed LIVE (dumping this page's compiled XData layout, then loading the real page with Playwright and screenshotting it) that no such thing exists. The only page-level chrome here is the "Menu" dropdown button (an absolutely-positioned %ZEN.Component.menu the plan already separately ruled out DOM-patching into - confirmed right, its own contextMenu content is server-sized) and a plain-text small-menu row - "Home | About | Save | Logout" - built by the overridable %OnGetSmallMenu(*pMenu) callback (every widget's OWN icon row - table/chart/dim-tree/print/export/search icons - is a per-widget thing already handled by BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot, not a page-level toolbar). Since there's no icon markup to model a new icon on, and %OnGetSmallMenu is a small, officially overridable server-side callback (confirmed live by dumping its compiled source: it just returns $ListBuild(caption,title,script) rows for the caller to render as text links) rather than a DOM structure to patch, this class adds "Export Dashboard" there instead - safer than a client-side DOM patch (no risk of the live-component property-read trap BIExport.UI.Widget.pivot had to work around, since nothing here reads a property off an already-rendered component at all) and consistent with how ANALYZERURL/viewerURL are also plain server-side overrides rather than client patches. GOTCHA hit writing this class (new, not previously documented): the stock %OnGetSmallMenu's formal spec, as dumped from the compiled class, shows its one parameter's passing mechanism as "*" (Output) - but writing the override's own formal spec using that same bare *pMenu shorthand made THIS ENTIRE CLASS fail to compile with a generic "ERROR #5559 ... non-matching {} or () ... or a missing ; character" parse error (confirmed by bisection: an otherwise-empty method with nothing but Quit in its body still failed with the exact same error, and swapping only the formal spec to the equivalent Output pMenu keyword form fixed it immediately, with no other change). Lesson: *name is how a compiled FormalSpec DISPLAYS an Output parameter after the fact, not necessarily valid UDL SOURCE syntax for declaring one in every context - prefer the explicit Output/ByRef keywords when writing a method by hand instead of guessing from a dumped signature.

Method.Description: The stock page's own ancestor (<class>%DeepSee.UserPortal.standardPage</class>) seeds the client-side <property>viewerURL</property> from <method>%DeepSee.UserPortal.Utils::%GetViewerURL</method>() - a hardcoded literal, "_DeepSee.UserPortal.DashboardViewer.zen" - inside ITS OWN <method>%OnAfterCreatePage</method> (confirmed live by dumping both methods' compiled source). Class.name: BIExport.XLSXWriter
Class.Description: Renders the normalized JSON structure produced by BIExport.MDXExport into a genuine .xlsx workbook (real cell types and number formats - not an HTML table saved with an .xls extension). Layout: the data sheet is a real Excel structured Table (native autofilter/banded rows, sortable, recognized as a table by Excel/other tools) starting at A1 - the header row is never pushed down by metadata. Title/subtitle/filters instead go on a separate "Info" sheet, plus the workbook's own document properties. BuildXLSX (single pivot/listing) and BuildMultiSheetXLSX (one workbook per dashboard, one sheet per pivot widget - see BIExport.DashboardExport) share the actual per-sheet writing logic via %WriteResultSheet, a private Language = python classmethod, rather than duplicating it - confirmed live, before writing either caller, that a live openpyxl Worksheet object built inside one Language = python classmethod can be passed as a plain argument into another Language = python classmethod of this same class (via iris.cls('BIExport.XLSXWriter')._WriteResultSheet(ws, data, table_name) - note the leading % becomes a leading _ for Python attribute access, confirmed the same way) and mutated there exactly as if the call had never left Python - no serialization, no loss of identity, Private classmethods included. That confirmation is what made the shared-helper approach (rather than duplicating this logic per the plan's own fallback) safe to build directly.

Method.name: IsAvailable
Method.Description: Two-tier check for whether BuildXLSX/BuildMultiSheetXLSX can actually run: plain ObjectScript (no Language = python), so it's safe to call from anywhere - a server-side gray-out check, a REST/CSP page's top-of-method guard, or a client-side ZenMethod round-trip - without dragging Python into the call chain just to answer "is Python even there." Confirmed live (see docs/iris-environment.md and CLAUDE.md's Embedded Python section) that ##class(%SYS.Python).Import(...) raises a catchable %Exception.PythonException on failure (e.g. ModuleNotFoundError for a missing package) rather than returning a %Status or writing to some other error channel - this method leans on that directly. Two distinct failure modes, each needing a different fix, so pReason is worded accordingly: - Import("sys") fails: Embedded Python itself isn't configured on this instance (the CPF PythonRuntimeLibrary/PythonRuntimeLibraryVersion parameters are empty or wrong) - a restart is required to pick up a CPF edit, so pReason says so rather than suggesting anything short of that. - Import("sys") succeeds but Import("openpyxl") fails: Python itself is fine, the package just isn't installed for whichever Python PythonRuntimeLibrary points at - pReason says to pip install openpyxl against that same Python. No caching - availability only changes via a CPF edit + restart (an extremely rare event relative to how often this gets called), and a fresh Import() on an already-loaded module is expected to be cheap; add caching later only if actually measured to matter.

Method.name: BuildXLSX
Method.Description: pJSON is the %ToJSON() output of a BIExport.MDXExport.BuildExportData() result. Returns the raw bytes of an .xlsx file.
Method.Implementation:
import json import io import openpyxl from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill import iris
data = json.loads(pJSON)
wb = openpyxl.Workbook() ws = wb.active ws.title = "Export"
INFO_TITLE_FONT = Font(bold=True, size=14, color="FFFFFF") INFO_TITLE_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="4472C4") INFO_LABEL_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="D9E1F2") INFO_NOTE_FONT = Font(italic=True, color="808080") HEADER_FONT = Font(bold=True)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Info sheet + document properties - title/subtitle/filters live here, never # inline on the data sheet, so the data sheet's header always starts at A1. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- title = data.get("title") or "" subtitle = data.get("subtitle") or "" cube = data.get("cube") or "" filters = data.get("filters") or []
info = wb.create_sheet("Info") info.sheet_view.showGridLines = False
info.cell(row=1, column=1, value="Export Info") info.cell(row=1, column=2, value="") info.merge_cells(start_row=1, start_column=1, end_row=1, end_column=2) for col in (1, 2): c = info.cell(row=1, column=col) c.font = INFO_TITLE_FONT c.fill = INFO_TITLE_FILL info.row_dimensions[1].height = 22
def info_label(row, text): c = info.cell(row=row, column=1, value=text) c.font = HEADER_FONT c.fill = INFO_LABEL_FILL
r = 3 if title: info_label(r, "Report") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=title) r += 1 if cube: info_label(r, "Cube") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=cube) r += 1 if subtitle: info_label(r, "Subtitle") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=subtitle) r += 1 for f in filters: info_label(r, f.get("name", "")) info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=f.get("value", "")) r += 1 if r == 3: c = info.cell(row=r, column=1, value="(no title, cube, subtitle, or filters supplied for this export)") c.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT info.column_dimensions["A"].width = 24 info.column_dimensions["B"].width = 50
if title: wb.properties.title = title if subtitle: wb.properties.description = subtitle if cube: wb.properties.subject = cube
notes = iris.cls('BIExport.XLSXWriter')._WriteResultSheet(ws, data, "ExportTable") for note in notes: note_cell = info.cell(row=info.max_row + 2, column=1, value=note) note_cell.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT
# Branding footer on the Info sheet - computed from info.max_row rather than a # manually-tracked counter, since earlier code writes a variable, optional number of # rows there (title/cube/subtitle/filters, plus any notes just above) and none of it # updates a shared "next free row" after writing. BRAND_LINK = "https://github.com/asinay/bi-export-plus" brand_row = info.max_row + 2 brand_cell = info.cell(row=brand_row, column=1, value="Generated with bi-export-plus") brand_cell.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT link_cell = info.cell(row=brand_row + 1, column=1, value=BRAND_LINK) link_cell.hyperlink = BRAND_LINK link_cell.font = Font(color="0563C1", underline="single")
buf = io.BytesIO() wb.save(buf) return buf.getvalue()

Method.name: BuildMultiSheetXLSX
Method.Description:
pJSON is the %ToJSON() output of a BIExport.DashboardExport.BuildDashboardExportData() result: {title, dashboardName, sheets:[{widgetName,title,data|error}], skipped:[...]}. Builds one combined "Info" sheet (dashboard title, a recap row per widget - sheet name, status, and any per-sheet note - plus the skipped-widgets list) and one data sheet per widget that has a "data" entry, via the same <method>%WriteResultSheet</method> helper <method>BuildXLSX</method> uses. A widget entry with an "error" instead of "data" (see <class>BIExport.DashboardExport</class>) gets a real sheet too, but with just that error message written on it rather than a Table/merged header - so the workbook always has exactly one sheet per pivot-family widget, whether or not that widget's own export succeeded, plus the Info sheet.
Returns the raw bytes of an .xlsx file.
Method.Implementation:
import json import io import openpyxl from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill import iris
data = json.loads(pJSON)
wb = openpyxl.Workbook() info = wb.active info.title = "Info" info.sheet_view.showGridLines = False
INFO_TITLE_FONT = Font(bold=True, size=14, color="FFFFFF") INFO_TITLE_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="4472C4") INFO_LABEL_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="D9E1F2") INFO_NOTE_FONT = Font(italic=True, color="808080") HEADER_FONT = Font(bold=True) ERROR_FONT = Font(color="C00000")
dashboard_title = data.get("title") or "" dashboard_name = data.get("dashboardName") or "" sheets = data.get("sheets") or [] skipped = data.get("skipped") or []
info.cell(row=1, column=1, value="Export Info") info.cell(row=1, column=2, value="") info.merge_cells(start_row=1, start_column=1, end_row=1, end_column=2) for col in (1, 2): c = info.cell(row=1, column=col) c.font = INFO_TITLE_FONT c.fill = INFO_TITLE_FILL info.row_dimensions[1].height = 22
def info_label(row, text): c = info.cell(row=row, column=1, value=text) c.font = HEADER_FONT c.fill = INFO_LABEL_FILL
r = 3 info_label(r, "Dashboard") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=dashboard_title or dashboard_name) r += 1 if dashboard_title and dashboard_name != dashboard_title: info_label(r, "Path") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=dashboard_name) r += 1 r += 1
info_label(r, "Widget") info.cell(row=r, column=2, value="Sheet") c = info.cell(row=r, column=3, value="Status") for col in (1, 2, 3): info.cell(row=r, column=col).font = HEADER_FONT r += 1
# Excel sheet-name rules (<=31 chars, none of []:*?/\, unique within the workbook) are # enforced by %SanitizeSheetName; used_names below is just this loop's own running list # so widget N+1's dedup sees widget N's already-chosen name. def sanitize_sheet_name(name, used): return iris.cls('BIExport.XLSXWriter')._SanitizeSheetName(name, used)
used_names = ["Info"]
for sheet_index, sheet_entry in enumerate(sheets, start=1): widget_name = sheet_entry.get("widgetName") or "" sheet_title = sheet_entry.get("title") or widget_name or "Sheet" sheet_name = sanitize_sheet_name(sheet_title, used_names) used_names.append(sheet_name)
ws = wb.create_sheet(sheet_name)
info.cell(row=r, column=1, value=widget_name) info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=sheet_name)
if "error" in sheet_entry: err_cell = ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value="Error exporting this widget:") err_cell.font = HEADER_FONT ws.cell(row=2, column=1, value=str(sheet_entry["error"])) ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 100 status_cell = info.cell(row=r, column=3, value="Error - see sheet") status_cell.font = ERROR_FONT else: # Excel Table names must be unique across the WHOLE workbook (not just per # sheet) - "Table_<n>" per widget guarantees that plus Excel's identifier rules # (alphanumeric/underscore, can't start with a digit), unlike the sheet's own # (arbitrary, sanitized-for-different-rules) display name. table_name = "Table_%d" % sheet_index notes = iris.cls('BIExport.XLSXWriter')._WriteResultSheet(ws, sheet_entry.get("data") or {}, table_name) info.cell(row=r, column=3, value="OK") for note in notes: r += 1 note_cell = info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=note) note_cell.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT r += 1
if not sheets: info.cell(row=r, column=1, value="(no pivot widgets found on this dashboard)") info.cell(row=r, column=1).font = INFO_NOTE_FONT r += 1
if skipped: r += 1 note_cell = info.cell(row=r, column=1, value="Skipped (not a pivot-family widget - chart/KPI/text widgets have " "no exportable pivot data of their own):") note_cell.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT r += 1 for sk in skipped: info.cell(row=r, column=1, value=sk.get("widgetName", "")) info.cell(row=r, column=2, value=sk.get("title", "") or sk.get("type", "")) r += 1
info.column_dimensions["A"].width = 24 info.column_dimensions["B"].width = 40 info.column_dimensions["C"].width = 18
if dashboard_title: wb.properties.title = dashboard_title
BRAND_LINK = "https://github.com/asinay/bi-export-plus" brand_row = info.max_row + 2 brand_cell = info.cell(row=brand_row, column=1, value="Generated with bi-export-plus") brand_cell.font = INFO_NOTE_FONT link_cell = info.cell(row=brand_row + 1, column=1, value=BRAND_LINK) link_cell.hyperlink = BRAND_LINK link_cell.font = Font(color="0563C1", underline="single")
buf = io.BytesIO() wb.save(buf) return buf.getvalue()

Method.name: %WriteResultSheet
Method.Description:
Shared per-sheet writer for one BuildExportData()-shaped `data` dict, used by both <method>BuildXLSX</method> (writing to its one "Export" sheet) and <method>BuildMultiSheetXLSX</method> (writing to one sheet per widget). Builds either a real Excel Table (the common case) or - when the column axis has more than one level (<var>colHeaderDepth</var> > 1) - a true merged multi-row header with no Table at all, exactly as the original single-sheet BuildXLSX always has (see the "Nested column headers" tradeoff in README.md). Returns a (possibly empty) list of plain-text notes the caller should surface somewhere on its own Info sheet - currently just the nested-header/no-Table explanation, when that branch is taken.
pWs is a live openpyxl Worksheet already created (and, other than its title, still blank) by the caller; this method writes into it directly and returns without saving or otherwise touching the workbook. pTableName is the Excel Table's displayName (only used when a real Table gets built at all - see the colHeaderDepth>1 branch below) - Excel requires Table names to be unique across the WHOLE workbook, not just per sheet, so a multi-sheet caller must pass a distinct name per widget; a single-sheet caller can just pass the fixed "ExportTable" name this always used before this method was extracted out of BuildXLSX.
Method.Implementation:
import datetime from openpyxl.styles import Font from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter from openpyxl.worksheet.table import Table, TableStyleInfo
ws = pWs data = pData notes = []
HEADER_FONT = Font(bold=True) col_widths = {}
def touch_width(col_idx, text): length = len(str(text)) if text is not None else 0 if length > col_widths.get(col_idx, 0): col_widths[col_idx] = length
def write_header(row, col, text): c = ws.cell(row=row, column=col, value=text) c.font = HEADER_FONT touch_width(col, text) return c
def apply_cell(r, c, cellobj): cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=c) if cellobj is None: return cell t = cellobj.get("t", "s") v = cellobj.get("v") fmt = cellobj.get("fmt") if t == "n": cell.value = v if fmt: cell.number_format = fmt elif t == "d": if v: try: cell.value = datetime.date.fromisoformat(v) except ValueError: cell.value = v cell.number_format = fmt or "mm/dd/yyyy" else: cell.value = "" elif t == "t": cell.value = (v or 0) / 86400.0 cell.number_format = fmt or "[h]:mm:ss" else: cell.value = v cell.number_format = "@" touch_width(c, v) return cell
def finalize_table(min_col, max_col, last_row, table_name, headers): """Wraps A1:.. through (min_col,max_col,last_row) as a real Excel Table. `headers` is the list of already-written header strings for min_col..max_col, used verbatim as the Table's column names (Excel requires these to match the header row cells).""" ref = "%s1:%s%d" % (get_column_letter(min_col), get_column_letter(max_col), last_row) tbl = Table(displayName=table_name, ref=ref) tbl.tableStyleInfo = TableStyleInfo(name="TableStyleMedium2", showRowStripes=True, showColumnStripes=False) tbl._initialise_columns() for col, name in zip(tbl.tableColumns, headers): col.name = str(name) if name else col.name ws.add_table(tbl) return tbl
def safe_name(name, fallback): return name if name else fallback
kind = data.get("kind", "cellset")
if kind == "listing": columns = data.get("columns", []) rows = data.get("rows", []) if not columns or not rows: ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value="No results") else: headers = [safe_name(c.get("name", ""), "Column%d" % (j + 1)) for j, c in enumerate(columns)] for j, h in enumerate(headers): write_header(1, j + 1, h) for i, data_row in enumerate(rows): for j, val in enumerate(data_row): ws.cell(row=2 + i, column=j + 1, value=val) touch_width(j + 1, val) last_row = 1 + len(rows) finalize_table(1, len(headers), last_row, pTableName or "ExportTable", headers) ws.freeze_panes = "A2" else: col_header_depth = data.get("colHeaderDepth", 0) row_header_depth = data.get("rowHeaderDepth", 0) col_count = data.get("colCount", 0) row_count = data.get("rowCount", 0) column_headers = data.get("columnHeaders", []) # outer level first, inner (measure) last row_headers = data.get("rowHeaders", []) row_header_names = data.get("rowHeaderNames", []) cells = data.get("cells", []) column_totals = data.get("columnTotals") row_totals = data.get("rowTotals") grand_total = data.get("grandTotal") # Excel's own totalsRowFunction vocabulary (ECMA-376): none/sum/min/max/average/ # count/countNums/stdDev/var/custom. Our aggregation keys match 1:1 except "avg" # (-> "average") and "pct" (% of total has no equivalent - "custom" means "not one # of Excel's built-in functions", which is accurate: there's no live formula behind # it, just the precomputed value). TOTALS_ROW_FUNCTION = {"sum": "sum", "count": "count", "min": "min", "max": "max", "avg": "average", "pct": "custom"} col_totals_row_function = TOTALS_ROW_FUNCTION.get(data.get("columnTotalAgg", "sum"), "custom") row_totals_row_function = TOTALS_ROW_FUNCTION.get(data.get("rowTotalAgg", "sum"), "custom")
if col_count == 0 or row_count == 0: ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value="No results") elif col_header_depth > 1: # A dimension on Columns needs a true 2+ row merged header - Excel's structured # Table feature requires exactly one header row, so this shape can't also be a # Table (see the "Nested column headers" tradeoff in README.md). Rather than # flatten the levels into one row (losing the visual grouping) to force a Table, # this branch keeps the real merged header and gives up the Table instead: # native autofilter/banded rows/tool-recognition, in exchange for an accurate # visual structure. Row-header column titles span every header row (merged # vertically); each column-header level gets its own row, merged horizontally # across runs of columns that share the same value at that level and every # shallower level (so a run never straddles an outer group's boundary). has_row_totals = row_totals is not None has_col_totals = column_totals is not None last_col = row_header_depth + col_count + (1 if has_row_totals else 0) header_rows = col_header_depth first_data_row = header_rows + 1
for k in range(row_header_depth): name = row_header_names[k] if k < len(row_header_names) else "" write_header(1, k + 1, safe_name(name, "Row %d" % (k + 1))) ws.merge_cells(start_row=1, start_column=k + 1, end_row=header_rows, end_column=k + 1)
def levels_match(a, b, upto): return all(column_headers[lv][a] == column_headers[lv][b] for lv in range(upto + 1))
for lvl in range(col_header_depth): row = lvl + 1 mergeable = lvl < col_header_depth - 1 j = 0 while j < col_count: k = j if mergeable: while k + 1 < col_count and levels_match(j, k + 1, lvl): k += 1 col = row_header_depth + 1 + j write_header(row, col, column_headers[lvl][j]) if k > j: ws.merge_cells(start_row=row, start_column=col, end_row=row, end_column=row_header_depth + 1 + k) j = k + 1
if has_row_totals: write_header(1, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, "Total") ws.merge_cells(start_row=1, start_column=row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, end_row=header_rows, end_column=row_header_depth + 1 + col_count)
# Data rows. for i in range(row_count): r = first_data_row + i hdrs = row_headers[i] if i < len(row_headers) else [] for k, label in enumerate(hdrs): ws.cell(row=r, column=k + 1, value=label) touch_width(k + 1, label) row_cells = cells[i] if i < len(cells) else [] for j, cellobj in enumerate(row_cells): apply_cell(r, row_header_depth + 1 + j, cellobj) if has_row_totals: apply_cell(r, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, row_totals[i])
last_data_row = first_data_row - 1 + row_count
if has_col_totals: totals_row_num = last_data_row + 1 if row_header_depth > 0: ws.cell(row=totals_row_num, column=row_header_depth, value="Total") for j, cellobj in enumerate(column_totals): apply_cell(totals_row_num, row_header_depth + 1 + j, cellobj) if has_row_totals and grand_total is not None: apply_cell(totals_row_num, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, grand_total) for c in range(1, last_col + 1): ws.cell(row=totals_row_num, column=c).font = HEADER_FONT
ws.freeze_panes = "%s%d" % (get_column_letter(row_header_depth + 1), first_data_row)
notes.append("'%s': this pivot has a dimension on Columns (multi-level column " "header), so its sheet keeps a true merged header instead of a " "flattened Excel Table - no autofilter/banded rows on this sheet." % ws.title) else: has_row_totals = row_totals is not None has_col_totals = column_totals is not None total_col_count = col_count + (1 if has_row_totals else 0) last_col = row_header_depth + total_col_count
# Header row (always row 1 - this is the whole point of the rewrite). row_headers_text = [] for k in range(row_header_depth): name = row_header_names[k] if k < len(row_header_names) else "" name = safe_name(name, "Row %d" % (k + 1)) row_headers_text.append(name) write_header(1, k + 1, name)
col_headers_text = [] for j in range(col_count): label = column_headers[0][j] if column_headers else "" col_headers_text.append(label) write_header(1, row_header_depth + 1 + j, label)
if has_row_totals: write_header(1, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, "Total")
# Data rows. for i in range(row_count): r = 2 + i hdrs = row_headers[i] if i < len(row_headers) else [] for k, label in enumerate(hdrs): ws.cell(row=r, column=k + 1, value=label) touch_width(k + 1, label) row_cells = cells[i] if i < len(cells) else [] for j, cellobj in enumerate(row_cells): apply_cell(r, row_header_depth + 1 + j, cellobj) if has_row_totals: apply_cell(r, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, row_totals[i])
last_data_row = 1 + row_count
totals_row_num = None if has_col_totals: totals_row_num = last_data_row + 1 # Matches the legacy exporter's convention: the "Total" label sits under # the last row-header column, the others in that row stay blank. if row_header_depth > 0: ws.cell(row=totals_row_num, column=row_header_depth, value="Total") for j, cellobj in enumerate(column_totals): apply_cell(totals_row_num, row_header_depth + 1 + j, cellobj) if has_row_totals and grand_total is not None: apply_cell(totals_row_num, row_header_depth + 1 + col_count, grand_total)
last_row = totals_row_num if totals_row_num else last_data_row all_headers = row_headers_text + col_headers_text + (["Total"] if has_row_totals else []) tbl = finalize_table(1, last_col, last_row, pTableName or "ExportTable", all_headers)
if totals_row_num: tbl.totalsRowShown = True tbl.totalsRowCount = 1 if row_header_depth > 0: tbl.tableColumns[row_header_depth - 1].totalsRowLabel = "Total" for j in range(col_count): tbl.tableColumns[row_header_depth + j].totalsRowFunction = col_totals_row_function if has_row_totals: tbl.tableColumns[row_header_depth + col_count].totalsRowFunction = row_totals_row_function for c in range(1, last_col + 1): ws.cell(row=totals_row_num, column=c).font = HEADER_FONT
ws.freeze_panes = "A2"
for idx, width in col_widths.items(): ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(idx)].width = min(max(width + 2, 8), 60)
return notes

Method.name: %SanitizeSheetName
Method.Description: Sanitizes+dedupes a candidate Excel sheet name: strips the characters Excel forbids in a sheet name ([ ] : * ? / \), truncates to Excel's 31-character limit, and - given the list of names already used earlier in the same workbook (pUsed, mutated in place is NOT relied on; caller re-appends the result itself) - appends " (2)", " (3)", etc. until the name is unique, re-truncating as needed so the suffixed form still fits in 31 characters.
Method.Implementation:
INVALID_CHARS = set('[]:*?/\\') base = ''.join(ch for ch in (pName or 'Sheet') if ch not in INVALID_CHARS).strip() if not base: base = 'Sheet' base = base[:31]
used_lower = set(u.lower() for u in (pUsed or [])) candidate = base n = 2 while candidate.lower() in used_lower: suffix = ' (%d)' % n candidate = base[:31 - len(suffix)] + suffix n += 1 return candidate
